To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the separation of anionic pharmaceutical compounds using ion exchange chromatography is well described by an isocratic model based on the concentration of the eluent anion and the percentage of an organic modifier in the solvent.
the effects of methanols on the retention of cations and anions on anion exchange columns can be described by simple mathematical models.
a model was developed to predict retention times and peak widths in the separation of anionic/cationic pharmaceutic compounds using mixed mode ion chromatography with a methanol gradient eluent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of predictive retention models for the ion chromatographic mixed-mode separation of anions and cations in the presence of methanol.

the development of a general model that can be used to predict the retention of anionic and/or cationic compounds in the mixed-mode separation of anions and cations on ion exchange columns using methanol as the organic modifier.
the use of ion chromatography for the separation of anionic/cationic compounds in pharmaceutical analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model presented here provides an excellent tool to allow for the prediction of the retention of a wide variety of anions and cations in the presence of methanol and an ionic eluent.

the retention of both anionic and cations in mixed-mode ion-exchange chromatography can be accurately predicted using a combination of empirical models based on the concentration of the ionic salt and the percentage of the organic modifier in the mobile phase, and that the peak compression model is adequate for estimating the peak width of analytes in these systems.

a simple empirical approach can provide a good description of the retention behaviour of a selection of cationic and anionic pharmaceutically related analytes under isocratic and gradient conditions using methanol and potassium hydroxide or methane sulfonic acid as the eluents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of methanol as an organic modifier in the ion chromatography of anionic and/or cationic analytes can be predicted with a high degree of accuracy and precision.

the models derived for retention prediction are capable of predicting analyte retention and peak width for a range of methanol and potassium hydroxide concentrations and gradient profiles with average prediction errors of less than 7% for retention time and 27% for peak width.

the models derived for the separation of the anionic and cations analyte mixtures are robust and can be used to predict retention time and peak widths under isocratic and gradient conditions over a broad range of methanol concentrations, including conditions where the analytes exhibit increased retention with increased methanol concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the retention behaviour of analytes can be predicted with reasonable accuracy using simple models that are based on the concentration of the ionic eluent and the concentration of the organic modifier in the mobile phase.
a single isocratic model can be used to predict retention times for a range of gradient elution profiles.
it is possible to predict analyte retention times for anion and cation mixtures under isocratic and gradient elution conditions using a limited number of experiments.
